profile.name: Aman Yadav
profile.tagline: I build RL environments, low-latency data pipelines, and the infrastructure that keeps them fast.
bio: I work close to the machine — the pipelines, the workers, the query plans. Most of what I enjoy is finding the one bottleneck that caps everything else, and moving it.

Right now I'm at Scaler AI Labs building production computer-use RL environments that ship to frontier labs for autonomous-agent training. Before that I was the sole engineer alongside the cofounder at Ticker360, taking an AI stock research platform from a landing page to 500+ users.
I'm in a dual-degree program at Scaler School of Technology and BITS Pilani, graduating 2027.

highlights: Built 10+ production-grade computer-use RL environments (Grafana, Sage, NetSuite, Zoho, Adobe) in Python and FastAPI, shipped to OpenAI / Meta / xAI for autonomous-agent training and evaluation.

Cut PII-scrubbing pipeline runtime 10x — 24 hrs to under 3 hrs on 5 TB of environment interaction data — by scaling the worker pool from 800 to 8,000. Unblocked the scale-up by replacing single-source manifest distribution with a tree-based fan-out (each tier seeding the next: 1 → 10 → 100 → …), eliminating the bandwidth bottleneck that had capped concurrency and enabling same-day handoff to partner labs.

Owned the Python capture/analysis backend and Next.js dashboard for a Tauri employee-activity monitoring desktop app (4-engineer team), ingesting periodic screenshots and OS accessibility (AX) trees to classify in-app user activity.

Ported the capture agent from macOS to Windows, where the native accessibility tree returned substantially sparser element data; restored macOS-level context fidelity by layering additional property and child-traversal queries per node, keeping the downstream activity classifier unchanged.

Designed analytics APIs over PostgreSQL and ClickHouse serving operator dashboards for large-scale workflow data, moving heavy aggregate queries off Postgres into ClickHouse to keep dashboard loads responsive as event volume grew.
Sole engineer alongside the cofounder on a greenfield AI stock research platform — took it from landing page to 500+ users, owning the Next.js frontend, Go backend, data pipelines, and deployment.

Built low-latency Golang (Gin) APIs over NASDAQ/NYSE equities, fetching concurrently from two market-data vendors via goroutine worker pools, backed by cron-scheduled MongoDB ingestion pipelines (prices, fundamentals, news) with indexing tuned to read patterns.

Built the Python AI research service — token-streamed chat and a tool-calling agent with database access — letting users query equities in plain English, with structured chart specs rendered as inline visualizations; served via ISR/SSG Next.js routes with access/refresh token auth. Dockerized on DigitalOcean.

projects.title: Conflux
projects.blurb: A real-time collaborative code editor where multiple people edit the same file without conflicts — CRDT sync under a VS Code-grade editing surface.
highlights: CRDT-based synchronization for conflict-free multi-user editing.
Room-based WebSocket architecture for low-latency collaborative sessions.
Monaco Editor integration for a VS Code-like experience in the browser.
Secure multi-language code execution via sandboxed execution APIs.

projects.title: CraveStream
projects.blurb: A TikTok-style food discovery platform — vertical video feeds, optimized media delivery, and hardened auth across a split Vercel/Render deployment.
highlights: Vertical video feed with optimized media delivery.
JWT auth over HttpOnly cookies to reduce XSS risk.
Role-based access control (RBAC) for users and content partners.
Solved CORS and distributed auth across Vercel and Render.
ImageKit integration for optimized storage and low-latency streaming.
